title: Fixed-Rate Interest Calculation for Home Comfort Financing Statements
content:
**Statement interest on fixed-rate Home Comfort Financing accounts.**

The fixed-rate closing interest charge is the fixed-rate interest base, multiplied by the fixed-rate charging rate and by the number of fixed-rate accrual days, divided by 100 and by 365, and rounded to the cent half up only at the end. The fixed-rate accrual days run from the day the previous interest charge posted, or from the funded date when none has posted, up to but not including the day this charge posts, and the fixed-rate interest base is applied to every one of those days. The fixed-rate interest base is the account balance on the day the charge posts, and the fixed-rate charging rate is the plan's APR.

## Elements

- **Interest base** — the account balance on the posting day, applied to every accrual day.
- **Charging rate** — the plan's APR (5.99, 7.99 or 9.99 percent, by plan), used unrounded.
- **Accrual days** — first day: the day the previous interest charge posted, or the funded date if no interest charge has posted; last day: the day before this charge posts.
- **Rounding** — once, on the final charge, to the cent half up.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs, a 120-Month 7.99% APR account)

*First closing charge.* Funded 14 August; first closing charge posts 1 September. No earlier interest charge, so the accrual days run from 14 August up to but not including 1 September: 18 days. Balance on 1 September: $12000.00. Charge: $12000.00 multiplied by 7.99 and by 18, divided by 100 and by 365, is $47.2832…, rounded half up: $47.28.

*Next closing charge.* Posts 1 October; the previous interest charge posted 1 September, so the accrual days run from 1 September up to but not including 1 October: 30 days. Balance on 1 October: $11890.55. Charge: $11890.55 multiplied by 7.99 and by 30, divided by 100 and by 365, is $78.0867…, rounded half up: $78.09.

## Points of judgement

- The posting day of one charge is the first accrual day of the next charge; no day is counted twice and none is skipped.
- The funded date is itself an accrual day of the first charge.
